questions.q: A pharmacist melts theobroma oil (cocoa butter) at too high a temperature while preparing rectal suppositories and cools it rapidly. The suppositories fail to solidify at room temperature (25°C) because an unstable polymorph formed. Which stable polymorph (melting at 34.5°C) should have been preserved?
questions.explanation: التسخين المفرط يحوّل زبدة الكاكاو لأشكال غير مستقرة تنصهر بدرجات منخفضة (18°C أو 22°C)، بينما الشكل المستقر بيتا (β) ينصهر عند 34.5°C وهو المثالي للتحاميل.

questions.q: A pharmaceutical company prepares an aqueous suspension of cortisone acetate using an unstable polymorphic form. During storage, the suspension develops severe caking of crystals. Why did this happen?
options: Unstable polymorphs of cortisone acetate convert to the stable polymorph in the presence of water, causing crystal growth and caking
Cortisone acetate dissolved completely in water
The suspension reached its critical temperature
Water lowered the melting point to 0°C
questions.explanation: أربع من أصل خمس أشكال لـ Cortisone acetate غير مستقرة بوجود الماء وتتحول للشكل المستقر مما يسبب تكتل البلورات (Caking)؛ لذا يجب استخدام الشكل المستقر قبل التحضير.

questions.q: Two generic brands of a slightly soluble antibiotic (chloramphenicol palmitate) have identical chemical formulas, yet Brand A shows much higher blood levels and therapeutic activity than Brand B. What physical pharmacy phenomenon explains this?
options: Polymorphism affecting the rate of drug dissolution
questions.explanation: في الأدوية قليلة الذوبان مثل Chloramphenicol palmitate، يؤثر تعدد الأشكال البلورية (Polymorphism) على سرعة الذوبان وبالتالي على الفعالية العلاجية.

questions.q: An asthma patient uses a pressurized metered-dose inhaler (pMDI). Inside the canister, the propellant is a liquid, but upon depressing the actuator valve, it expels a fine drug spray. What happens if the canister is accidentally heated above the propellant's critical temperature (Tc)?
options: The propellant can no longer exist as a liquid regardless of the pressure inside the canister
The propellant freezes into a crystalline solid
The vapor pressure drops to zero
The drug precipitates as a dimer
questions.explanation: فوق درجة الحرارة الحرجة (Tc) يستحيل وجود المادة كسائل مهما كان الضغط المسلط داخل العبوة.

questions.q: A pharmaceutical manufacturer wants to extract a heat-sensitive active herbal compound and remove caffeine from a botanical extract without using toxic organic solvents. Which state of matter is ideal for this process?
questions.explanation: الموائع فوق الحرجة (Supercritical fluids) مثالية للاستخلاص والتنقية بدرجات حرارة منخفضة ونزع الكافيين وتقليل السمية.

questions.q: A laboratory technician in a high-altitude mountain city boils water to sterilize glassware and notices it boils at 94°C instead of 100°C. What is the physical reason?
options: Lower atmospheric pressure at higher elevation lowers the boiling point
Water forms stronger hydrogen bonds at high altitude
Higher atmospheric pressure raises the boiling point
questions.explanation: في المرتفعات يقل الضغط الجوي، فيتساوى ضغط بخار الماء مع الضغط الخارجي عند درجة حرارة أقل من 100°C.

questions.q: A pharmacist stores a volatile liquid anesthetic (diethyl ether) and an aqueous solution in identical closed bottles at 30°C. Which bottle develops much higher internal vapor pressure and why?
options: Diethyl ether, because it has weaker intermolecular attractive forces than water
Water, because hydrogen bonding increases vapor pressure
Both have identical vapor pressures at 30°C
questions.explanation: الإيثر له قوى تجاذب ضعيفة مقارنة بالأواصر الهيدروجينية القوية في الماء، لذلك يتبخر بسهولة أكبر ويعطي ضغط بخار أعلى بكثير.

questions.q: A formulation scientist mixes phenol and water (35% w/w phenol) at room temperature (25°C) and observes two separate liquid layers. How can the scientist convert this mixture into a single clear homogeneous phase without adding a third solvent?
options: Heat the mixture above its Upper Critical Solution Temperature (66.8°C)
Add NaCl to make it isotonic
questions.explanation: درجة حرارة المحلول الحرجة العليا لنظام الفينول والماء هي 66.8°C، وعند التسخين فوقها يمتزجان تماماً في طور واحد.

questions.q: A hospital nurse accidentally infuses pure sterile distilled water (0% NaCl) intravenously into a patient instead of 0.9% normal saline. What dangerous effect occurs to the patient's red blood cells?
options: Water rushes into RBCs causing swelling and hemolysis (rupture) with hemoglobin release
No change occurs because water is neutral
questions.explanation: الماء المقطر منخفض التوتر (Hypotonic) مقارنة بالدم، فيدخل الماء إلى كريات الدم الحمراء مسبباً انتفاخها وانفجارها (Hemolysis).

questions.q: A patient receives an accidental rapid infusion of a hypertonic 2.0% NaCl solution. What happens to the red blood cells exposed to this solution?
options: Water moves out of the RBCs, causing them to shrink and wrinkle (crenation)
Water moves into the RBCs, causing hemolysis
questions.explanation: محلول 2.0% NaCl عالي التوتر (Hypertonic)، فيسحب الماء من داخل كريات الدم الحمراء فتتكمش وتتجعد (Crenation).

questions.q: A patient with uncontrolled Type 1 diabetes is brought to the emergency department in diabetic coma. Arterial blood gas reveals a life-threatening blood pH of 6.8. Which primary plasma buffer system is immediately working to resist this severe drop in pH?
options: Carbonic acid / bicarbonate and sodium phosphate buffers
questions.explanation: في غيبوبة السكري قد يهبط pH الدم إلى 6.8 (تحت الحد الخطير 6.9)، وتعمل البفرات الأولية بالبلازما (الكربونيك/بيكربونات وفوسفات الصوديوم) لمقاومة هذا الهبوط.

questions.q: A patient with metabolic acidosis has a blood pH below 7.4. How do the kidneys compensate to restore acid-base balance?
options: By excreting excess H+ ions into the urine
By retaining H+ ions in the blood
By secreting NaOH into the bloodstream
questions.explanation: عندما ينخفض pH الدم دون الطبيعي (< 7.4)، تقوم الكلى بطرح أيونات الهيدروجين (H+) في الإدرار.

questions.q: A pharmacist is formulating an oral pediatric syrup and considers using a borate buffer because it is inexpensive. Why must this choice be rejected?
options: Borate buffer has toxic effects and must not be used for oral or parenteral products
Borate buffer cannot dissolve in water
Borate buffer has a pKa of 1.0
questions.explanation: بفر البورات سام (Toxic) لذلك يُمنع استخدامه في المستحضرات الفموية (Oral) أو الحقنية (Parenteral).

questions.q: An ophthalmologist notices that patients complain of stinging and redness when using an eye drop buffered at pH 5.5 with high-capacity phosphate buffer, whereas another eye drop at pH 5.0 in boric acid causes no discomfort. Why?
options: Boric acid has a low buffer capacity so tears easily neutralize it to pH 7.4, whereas high-capacity phosphate resists neutralization
Boric acid is a strong base
questions.explanation: حامض البوريك ذو سعة تنظيمية منخفضة فتستطيع الدموع معادلته بسهولة، بينما بفر الفوسفات عالي السعة يقاوم المعادلة ويسبب تهيّج العين.

questions.q: A pharmacist formulates a pilocarpine (weak base, pKb = 7.15) eye drop. If the formulation pH is raised too high (e.g., pH 8.5) during storage, what problem will occur in the bottle?
options: Excess unionized free base forms, exceeding its limited water solubility and precipitating out of solution
The drug becomes 100% ionized and more soluble
The drug converts into a strong acid
questions.explanation: رفع الـ pH لمحلول قاعدة ضعيفة يزيد نسبة القاعدة الحرة (B) قليلة الذوبان بالماء، وعندما تتجاوز حد ذوبانيتها تترسب في العبوة.

questions.q: Why does instilling an acidic pilocarpine HCl eye drop (low buffer capacity, pH ~4–5) still result in good drug absorption across the lipid corneal membrane?
options: Tears (pH ~7.4) gradually neutralize the low-capacity drop, converting ionized salt (BH+) into lipid-soluble unionized base (B)
The ionized salt (BH+) crosses the lipid bilayer faster than the free base
The cornea only absorbs water-soluble ions
questions.explanation: الدموع (pH 7.4) تعادل القطرة تدريجياً (لأن سعتها التنظيمية منخفضة) فتحوّل الملح المتأين (BH+) إلى قاعدة حرة غير متأينة (B) ذائبة بالدهون وتعبر القرنية بسهولة.

questions.q: A pharmacist needs to prepare a buffer at target pH 4.8. Four weak acids are available with pKa values of 2.1, 4.76, 7.2, and 9.3. Which weak acid should be chosen for maximum buffer capacity?
questions.explanation: للحصول على أعلى سعة تنظيمية يجب اختيار حامض ضعيف تكون قيمة pKa له أقرب ما يمكن إلى الـ pH المطلوب (4.76 ≈ 4.8).

questions.q: A pharmacist prepares a 100 mL isotonic eye drop containing 1 g of ephedrine sulfate (E = 0.23). If the patient is on a strict sodium-free regimen and dextrose (E = 0.16) is used instead of NaCl, how much dextrose must be added?
questions.explanation: النقص المكافئ لـ NaCl هو 0.90 - 0.23 = 0.67 g؛ وبقسمته على E للدكستروز (0.16) نحتاج 4.2 g دكستروز.

questions.q: A compounding pharmacist prepares 30 mL of 1% procaine HCl (E = 0.21) using the White-Vincent method. After dissolving 0.3 g of procaine HCl in 7.0 mL of purified water, the assistant accidentally adds 23 mL of pure distilled water to reach 30 mL. What is the resulting tonicity?
options: Hypotonic, because pure water diluted the isotonic 7.0 mL solution instead of using an isotonic diluting vehicle
questions.explanation: إضافة ماء مقطر لإكمال الحجم تخفف المحلول وتجعله منخفض التوتر (Hypotonic)؛ يجب الإكمال بمذيب متساوي التوتر (Isotonic diluent).

questions.q: A pharmacy student measures the pH of an unbuffered purified water sample using a colorimetric pH indicator paper and gets an inaccurate reading. Why is the colorimetric method unreliable for unbuffered solutions?
options: The indicator itself is a weak acid or base and alters the pH of the unbuffered solution
Purified water has a buffer capacity above 0.2
questions.explanation: الدليل اللوني نفسه عبارة عن حامض أو قاعدة ضعيفة، فيغيّر pH المحلول غير المنظم ويعطي قراءة غير دقيقة.

questions.q: A hospital pharmacist checks the freezing point of a newly compounded ophthalmic solution and finds it freezes at -0.35°C. What does this indicate about the solution?
options: It is hypotonic (freezing point depression < 0.52°C) and requires a tonicity-adjusting agent
It is hypertonic and needs dilution
questions.explanation: لأن درجة الانجماد -0.35°C (أقل انخفاضاً من -0.52°C للدموع)، فالمحلول منخفض التوتر (Hypotonic) ويحتاج لإضافة عامل تعديل توترية.

questions.q: A parenteral injection has a pH of 4.0 (far from blood pH 7.4) for drug stability. To minimize pain and tissue irritation upon injection, how should the pharmacist design the formulation?
options: Use a low buffer capacity and the smallest practical injection volume
Use a very high buffer capacity and a large 10 mL volume
Use a basic buffer made from ammonia
questions.explanation: لتقليل الألم وتهيّج الأنسجة عند وجود فرق كبير بالـ pH، نستخدم سعة تنظيمية منخفضة وأصغر حجم ممكن للحقنة.

questions.q: A pharmacist stores a basic buffer solution (NH3 / NH4+) in a warm room (40°C) instead of 20°C and notices a significant drop in its pH, whereas an acetate buffer stored in the same room barely changes. Why?
options: Basic buffers depend on pKw, which changes markedly with temperature
Acetate buffers are immune to Kw because they are strong acids
Acetic acid evaporates faster than ammonia
questions.explanation: معادلة البفر القاعدي تعتمد على pKw الذي يتغير بوضوح مع درجة الحرارة، بعكس البفر الحامضي.

questions.q: A chemist adds a large amount of NaCl (neutral salt) to a phosphate buffer solution and measures a slight shift in pH. What is the physical explanation?
options: Increased ionic strength reduces the activity coefficients (γ < 1) of the buffer ions
NaCl reacts chemically with water to form HCl
NaCl acts as a strong base
questions.explanation: إضافة ملح متعادل تزيد القوة الأيونية وتقلل معاملات الفعالية (γ) لأيونات البفر مما يسبب تغيراً طفيفاً في الـ pH.

questions.q: A quality control analyst wants to determine the approximate molecular weight of a new volatile liquid anesthetic. They vaporize 0.30 g of it in a 200 mL flask at 1 atm and 100°C. Which law allows them to calculate M?
questions.explanation: يمكن إيجاد الوزن الجزيئي التقريبي لبخار مادة متطايرة باستخدام قانون الغاز المثالي: M = gRT / PV.

questions.q: A pharmacist needs a single buffer system that can maintain nearly constant buffer capacity across a very wide pH range (from pH 3 to pH 11) for an analytical dissolution study. What should they prepare?
options: A universal buffer combining multiple buffers with overlapping pKa values
questions.explanation: البفر الشامل (Universal buffer) يدمج عدة بفرات بقيم pKa متداخلة ليعطي سعة تنظيمية ثابتة تقريباً على مدى واسع (3–11).

questions.q: In a pharmacy lab, adding sodium acetate to an acetic acid solution causes the pH to rise and the degree of ionization of acetic acid to drop. What principle is demonstrated?
questions.explanation: إضافة أيون الأسيتات المشترك (Ac-) تزيح التوازن لليسار وتقلل تأين حامض الخليك، وهذا هو تأثير الأيون المشترك (Common ion effect).

questions.q: A pharmacist is calculating the E value for a newly synthesized uni-univalent drug salt (MW = 187, Liso = 3.4) that is not listed in standard tables. What E value will they calculate?
questions.explanation: بتطبيق معادلة E ≈ 17 × (Liso / MW) = 17 × 3.4 / 187 = 0.31.

questions.q: A patient uses an ophthalmic solution of apomorphine HCl (1%, 100 mL, ΔTf 1% = 0.08°C). Using the cryoscopic method (ΔTf 1% NaCl = 0.58°C), how much NaCl must the pharmacist add to prevent eye irritation from hypotonicity?
questions.explanation: النقص المتبقي = 0.52 - 0.08 = 0.44°C، وبقسمته على 0.58 نحصل على 0.76 g NaCl لكل 100 مل.

questions.q: A drug formulation contains an oily liquid immiscible with water, an aqueous phase, and solid undissolved drug crystals at the bottom. How many phases (P) are present in this condensed system?
options: 3 phases (oil phase + water phase + solid drug phase)
questions.explanation: السائلان غير الممتزجين يشكلان طورين منفصلين، بالإضافة إلى الدواء الصلب غير المذاب كطور ثالث، فالمجموع 3 أطوار.

questions.q: A patient with severe vomiting loses stomach acid (HCl) and develops metabolic alkalosis (blood pH > 7.4). How do the kidneys respond to help normalize blood pH?
questions.explanation: عندما يرتفع pH الدم فوق 7.4 (قلوية)، تحتفظ الكلى بأيونات الهيدروجين (H+ retained) لإعادة التوازن.

questions.q: A pharmacist dilutes a sample of human tears 1:10 with neutral distilled water during a lab test and notices no change in pH. Why?
options: Tears have a high buffer capacity and tolerate up to 1:15 dilution with neutral water before pH changes
Distilled water has a pH of 7.4
questions.explanation: الدموع تمتلك سعة تنظيمية عالية تسمح بتخفيف يصل إلى 1:15 بالماء المقطر المتعادل دون تغير ملحوظ في الـ pH.

questions.q: A researcher prepares a 0.02 M total concentration acetate buffer at pH = pKa (4.76) for a stability test. What is the maximum buffer capacity (βmax) of this solution?
Why does a weakly acidic drug (like aspirin, HA) cross the lipid gastric mucosa more readily at the low pH of the stomach (~2) than in the alkaline intestine?
options: At low pH, the weak acid exists predominantly in its unionized, lipid-soluble molecular form (HA)
At low pH, the weak acid is 100% ionized
Stomach acid destroys the lipid bilayer
questions.explanation: في الوسط الحامضي للمعدة (pH ~2) يبقى الحامض الضعيف بشكل جزيئي غير متأين (HA) ذائب في الدهون فيعبر الأغشية بسهولة.

questions.q: A compounding pharmacist prepares a 100 mL isotonic eye drop containing TWO ingredients: 0.06 g phenacaine HCl (E = 0.20) and 0.3 g boric acid (E = 0.50). Using White-Vincent, how much sterile distilled water is first added to dissolve the drugs into an isotonic solution?
options: 18 mL (then complete to 100 mL with an isotonic diluting vehicle)
questions.explanation: V = [(0.06 × 0.20) + (0.3 × 0.50)] × 111.1 = 18 mL ماء مقطر، ثم يُكمل الحجم إلى 100 mL بمذيب متساوي التوتر.
